title: 2022 building code energy and accessibility standards adopted (the Northern Territory)
summary: The Northern Territory applied the NCC 2022 livable housing and condensation provisions from 1 October 2023, with housing energy efficiency kept at 5 stars.

instruments.title: National Construction Code 2022 (residential energy efficiency and livable housing) as adopted in the Northern Territory
instruments.provisions: state adoption of NCC 2022 Volume Two and the Livable Housing Design Standard (instrument not checked)

commenced.what: NCC 2022 livable housing and condensation provisions applied; housing energy efficiency limited to 5 stars

direction_rationale: The 2022 code raised minimum energy performance for new homes to 7 stars and added livable housing design requirements. Design and compliance costs are partly fixed per dwelling and may fall hardest on small builders, lowering entry and raising exit.
comparison: Staggered and partial adoption 2023-2025 (NSW and WA did not adopt the livable housing provisions)

assessment.summary: Adopts the 2022 National Construction Code's higher energy efficiency (7-star) and livable housing standards for new homes. The Northern Territory kept energy efficiency at 5 stars and adopted only livable housing and condensation rules. The standards cut running costs and improve access, which are not weighed here; they also add to the cost of building.

marks.reason: Adds design and compliance costs to every new home, which weigh most on small builders.
Adopting only part of the national code, or a local version, leaves builders working across states with different rules.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission estimates housing construction regulation costs about 1% of GDP a year.
